same_original_doodle_identity.assessment: The keys remain recognizably the supplied original doodle: angular large head, uneven outlined ears, the distinctive unequal eye shapes, connected angular face and muzzle, short bent nose, and sparse angular torso marks. The omitted tail is appropriate to this close source crop. No new rendering style is needed.

source_pose_event.assessment: The source contact sheet shows an actual head bow and turn down-left, a low hold, then a return toward the camera. The key sequence conveys leftward travel and return, but the low keys still present essentially the same upright face. In source-04 through source-08 the eyes and muzzle sit down along the leftward-facing head, with the near right ear high and the far side compressed. In key-04 through key-08 the recognizable face remains high in an upright head and both ears remain broadly presented. The sampled event therefore reads more as sideways relocation and resizing than the source's bowed head and changed orientation. This judgment concerns the sampled poses only, not playback.

source_crop_part_honesty.assessment: The keys retain the close head-and-upper-body crop, leave the torso cut by the lower and left edges, and omit the original doodle's off-crop tail and lower body. No added visible limb or tail invents an event absent from this retained source interval. Exact head-to-shoulder relationships still need the pose repair described below.

actually_viewed_normal_speed_motion.assessment: I viewed the supplied static images. most_important_gap: The central down-left bow is not embodied in the low head poses: the doodle's face stays upright and high while the whole head moves left. This loses the source event even though the original doodle identity survives.

Preserve the sampled leftward displacement and the return-to-camera endpoint. Then obtain an actual normal-speed comparison review; this review cannot close that separate evidence requirement.
